p2.original: When you were younger did you babysit, deliver papers, or mow the lawn for money? If so, you faced stiff competition from many other competitors who offered identical services. There was nothing to stop others from also offering their services.
p2.zh: 你年轻的时候是照看孩子的 还是送文件的 还是为了钱割草坪的? 如果是的话,你就会面临来自许多其他竞争者的激烈竞争,他们提供同样的服务。没有任何东西可以阻止其他人也提供服务。

p3.original: All of you charged the “going rate.” If you tried to charge more, your customers would simply buy from someone else. These conditions are very similar to the conditions agricultural growers face.
p3.zh: 所有人都向“现行”收费。 如果你试图收取更多的费用,你的顾客就会从别人那里买东西。 这些条件与农业种植者所面临的条件非常相似.

p4.original: Growing a crop may be more difficult to start than a babysitting or lawn mowing service, but growers face the same fierce competition. In the grand scale of world agriculture, farmers face competition from thousands of others because they sell an identical product. After all, winter wheat is winter wheat, but if they find it hard to make money with that crop, it is relatively easy for farmers to leave the marketplace for another crop. In this case, they do not sell the family farm, they switch crops.
p4.zh: 种植作物可能比做保姆或割草服务更难开始,但种植者面临同样的激烈竞争.在世界农业的庞大规模中,农民面临数千人的竞争,因为他们销售一种相同的产品。毕竟,冬季小麦是冬季小麦,但是如果他们觉得用这种作物赚钱很困难,农民离开市场换另一种作物比较容易. 在这种情况下,他们不出售家庭农场,而是交换作物。

p5.original: Take the case of the upper Midwest region of the United States—for many generations the area was called “King Wheat.” According to the United States Department of Agriculture National Agricultural Statistics Service, statistics by state, in 1997, 11.6 million acres of wheat and 780,000 acres of corn were planted in North Dakota. In the intervening 25 or so years has the mix of crops changed? Since it is relatively easy to switch crops, did farmers change what they planted in response to changes in relative crop prices? We will find out at chapter’s end.
p5.zh: 以美国中西部地区为例——在许多代人中,该地区被称为 " 小麦王 " 。 据美国农业部国家农业统计局的统计,1997年,在北达科他州种植了1,160万英亩的小麦和78万英亩的玉米。 在中间的25年左右中,农作物的混合情况有变化吗? 由于相对容易转换作物,农民是否根据相对作物价格的变化而改变种植方式? 我们将在章尾找到答案。

p6.original: In the meantime, let's consider the topic of this chapter—the perfectly competitive market. This is a market in which entry and exit are relatively easy and competitors are “a dime a dozen.”
p6.zh: 同时,让我们来考虑本章的主题,即完全具有竞争力的市场。 这是一个市场,在这个市场中,出入境相对容易,竞争者“十几分钱”。

p13.original: Most businesses face two realities: no one is required to buy their products, and even customers who might want those products may buy from other businesses instead. Firms that operate in perfectly competitive markets face this reality. In this chapter, you will learn how such firms make decisions about how much to produce, how much profit they make, whether to stay in business or not, and many others. Industries differ from one another in terms of how many sellers there are in a specific market, how easy or difficult it is for a new firm to enter, and the type of products that they sell. Economists refer to this as an industry's market structure. In this chapter, we focus on perfect competition. However, in other chapters we will examine other industry types: Monopoly and Monopolistic Competition and Oligopoly.
p13.zh: 大多数企业面临两个现实:没有人需要购买其产品,即使可能想要这些产品的客户也可以从其他企业购买。 在竞争激烈的市场上经营的公司正面临着这一现实。 在本章中,你们将了解这些公司如何决定生产多少,利润多少,是否继续经营,以及许多其他公司。不同行业在具体市场有多少销售者,新公司进入有多容易或有多难,以及它们销售的产品种类方面,各有不同.经济学家将此称为行业的市场结构. 在本章中,我们侧重于完美的竞争. 然而,在其他章节中,我们将审查其他行业类型:垄断和垄断竞争和奥利戈波利。

p14.original: Perfect Competition and Why It Matters
p14.zh: 完美的竞争和为什么它很重要

p15.original: Firms are in perfect competition when the following conditions occur: (1) many firms produce identical products; (2) many buyers are available to buy the product, and many sellers are available to sell the product; (3) sellers and buyers have all relevant information to make rational decisions about the product that they are buying and selling; and (4) firms can enter and leave the market without any restrictions—in other words, there is free entry and exit into and out of the market.
p15.zh: 在出现下列条件时,公司处于完美的竞争之中:(1) 许多公司生产相同的产品;(2) 许多买家可以购买产品,许多卖家可以出售产品;(3) 卖家和买家拥有一切相关信息,可以对其买卖的产品作出合理的决定;(4) 公司可以不受任何限制地进出市场——换句话说,可以自由进出市场。

p16.original: A perfectly competitive firm is known as a price taker, because the pressure of competing firms forces it to accept the prevailing equilibrium price in the market. If a firm in a perfectly competitive market raises the price of its product by so much as a penny, it will lose all of its sales to competitors. When a wheat grower, as we discussed in the Bring It Home feature, wants to know the going price of wheat, they have to check on the computer or listen to the radio. Supply and demand in the entire market solely determine the market price, not the individual farmer. A perfectly competitive firm must be a very small player in the overall market, so that it can increase or decrease output without noticeably affecting the overall quantity supplied and price in the market.
p16.zh: 一个完全具有竞争力的公司被称为一个价格承担者,因为竞争公司的压力迫使它接受市场中普遍存在的平衡价格。 如果一个完全具有竞争力的市场中的公司将其产品的价格提高一分钱,它就会失去对竞争对手的所有销售。 一个小麦种植者,正如我们在《带回家》的专辑中所讨论的, 想知道小麦的价格, 他们必须检查电脑或者听收音机。整个市场的供求只能决定市场价格,而不是农民个人。 一个完全有竞争力的公司必须是整个市场上很小的参与者,这样它就可以增加或减少产出,而不会明显地影响市场供应的总数量和价格。

p17.original: A perfectly competitive market is a hypothetical extreme; however, producers in a number of industries do face many competitor firms selling highly similar goods, in which case they must often act as price takers. Economists often use agricultural markets as an example. The same crops that different farmers grow are largely interchangeable. According to the United States Department of Agriculture monthly reports, in December 2021, U.S. corn farmers received an average of $5.47 per bushel. A corn farmer who attempted to sell at $6.00 per bushel would not have found any buyers. A perfectly competitive firm will not sell below the equilibrium price either. Why should they when they can sell all they want at the higher price? Other examples of agricultural markets that operate in close to perfectly competitive markets are small roadside produce markets and small organic farmers.
p17.zh: 完全具有竞争力的市场是一种假设的极端;然而,一些行业的生产者确实面临许多竞争企业,它们销售的商品非常相似,在这种情况下,它们必须经常充当价格的承受者。经济学家经常以农业市场为例.与不同农民种植的相同作物基本上可以互换。 根据美国农业部的月度报告,2021年12月,美国玉米种植者平均每株灌木获得5.47美元.试图以每棵灌木林6美元的价格出售玉米的农民不会找到任何买家。 一个完全有竞争力的公司也不会销售低于平衡价格。 当他们可以以更高的价格出售他们想要的一切时,他们为什么要卖呢? 在接近完全竞争的市场上运作的农业市场的其他例子包括小路边产品市场和小有机农户。

p18.zh: 访问这个显示各种商品目前价值的网站。

p19.original: This chapter examines how profit-seeking firms decide how much to produce in perfectly competitive markets. Such firms will analyze their costs as we discussed in the chapter on Production, Costs and Industry Structure. In the short run, the perfectly competitive firm will seek the quantity of output where profits are highest or, if profits are not possible, where losses are lowest.
p19.zh: 本章审查营利性公司如何决定在完全有竞争力的市场上生产多少。此类公司将按照我们在关于生产、成本和工业结构的一章中的讨论,分析其成本。在短期内,完全具有竞争力的公司将寻求利润最高或如果不可能获得利润,损失最低的产出数量。

p20.original: In the long run, positive economic profits will attract competition as other firms enter the market. Economic losses will cause firms to exit the market. Ultimately, perfectly competitive markets will attain long-run equilibrium when no new firms want to enter the market and existing firms do not want to leave the market, as economic profits have been driven down to zero.
p20.zh: 从长远来看,随着其他公司进入市场,积极的经济利润将吸引竞争。经济损失将导致企业退出市场.最终,如果没有任何新的公司想进入市场,现有公司不愿意离开市场,完全具有竞争力的市场将实现长期平衡,因为经济利润已经降到零。

p22.original: A perfectly competitive firm is a price taker, which means that it must accept the equilibrium price at which it sells goods. If a perfectly competitive firm attempts to charge even a tiny amount more than the market price, it will be unable to make any sales. In a perfectly competitive market there are thousands of sellers, easy entry, and identical products. A short-run production period is when firms are producing with some fixed inputs. Long-run equilibrium in a perfectly competitive industry occurs after all firms have entered and exited the industry and seller profits are driven to zero.
p22.zh: 完全具有竞争力的公司是价格的承受者,这意味着它必须接受其销售商品的平衡价格。 如果一个完全有竞争力的公司试图收取甚至比市场价格高的微小数额,它将无法进行任何销售。在一个完全竞争的市场上,有成千上万的销售商,容易进入,以及相同的产品。短期生产期是企业用某些固定投入进行生产。在一个完全具有竞争力的行业中,所有公司都进入和退出该行业,销售利润被推向零后,就出现了长期平衡。

p23.original: Perfect competition means that there are many sellers, there is easy entry and exiting of firms, products are identical from one seller to another, and sellers are price takers.
p23.zh: 完美的竞争意味着有许多销售商,公司进出容易,产品在卖方之间是相同的,卖方是价格承担者。

p25.original: Firms in a perfectly competitive market are said to be “price takers”—that is, once the market determines an equilibrium price for the product, firms must accept this price. If you sell a product in a perfectly competitive market, but you are not happy with its price, would you raise the price, even by a cent?
p25.zh: 在一个完全竞争的市场上的公司据说是 " 价格承受者 " ,即一旦市场决定了产品的平衡价格,公司就必须接受这一价格。 如果你在一个完全竞争的市场中销售产品,但是你对它的价格不满意,你会提高价格,甚至提高一美分吗?

p26.original: No, you would not raise the price. Your product is exactly the same as the product of the many other firms in the market. If your price is greater than that of your competitors, then your customers would switch to them and stop buying from you. You would lose all your sales.
p26.zh: 不,你不会提高价格。 你的产品和市场上许多其他公司的产品完全一样. 如果你的价格比竞争者高, 你的客户会转手 并停止从你购买。 你会失去所有的销售额。

p27.original: Would independent trucking fit the characteristics of a perfectly competitive industry?
p27.zh: 独立的卡车运输是否符合一个完全有竞争力的行业的特点?

p28.original: Possibly. Independent truckers are by definition small and numerous. All that is required to get into the business is a truck (not an inexpensive asset, though) and a commercial driver’s license. To exit, one need only sell the truck. All trucks are essentially the same, providing transportation from point A to point B. (We’re assuming we not talking about specialized trucks.) Independent truckers must take the going rate for their service, so independent trucking does seem to have most of the characteristics of perfect competition.
p28.zh: 也许吧独立卡车司机人数不多,数量众多。进入企业只需要一辆卡车(不是廉价资产)和商业驾驶执照。 要出口,只需要卖掉卡车 所有卡车基本相同,提供从A点到B点的运输.(我们假设我们不谈专业卡车。 ) 独立卡车手必须按其服务率,因此独立的卡车似乎具有完美竞争的大部分特征。

p30.original: A single firm in a perfectly competitive market is relatively small compared to the rest of the market. What does this mean? How “small” is “small”?
p30.zh: 与市场其他部分相比,在竞争完全激烈的市场上的一家公司相对较小。 这是什么意思?“小”是怎样的?

p31.original: What are the four basic assumptions of perfect competition? Explain in words what they imply for a perfectly competitive firm.
p31.zh: 完美竞争的四个基本假设是什么? 用语言解释它们对于一个完全有竞争力的公司意味着什么.

It is hard to think of this process as being part of a very complex market, with a demand and a supply for partners. p36.zh: 竞争企业如何作出产出决定

p37.original: A perfectly competitive firm has only one major decision to make—namely, what quantity to produce. To understand this, consider a different way of writing out the basic definition of profit:
p37.zh: 完全具有竞争力的公司只有一个主要的决定,即生产多少数量。 为了理解这一点,考虑用另一种方式来写出利润的基本定义:

p38.original: Since a perfectly competitive firm must accept the price for its output as determined by the product’s market demand and supply, it cannot choose the price it charges. This is already determined in the profit equation, and so the perfectly competitive firm can sell any number of units at exactly the same price. It implies that the firm faces a perfectly elastic demand curve for its product: buyers are willing to buy any number of units of output from the firm at the market price. When the perfectly competitive firm chooses what quantity to produce, then this quantity—along with the prices prevailing in the market for output and inputs—will determine the firm’s total revenue, total costs, and ultimately, level of profits.
p38.zh: 由于一个完全有竞争力的公司必须接受由该产品的市场供求决定的其产出价格,因此它不能选择它收取的价格。 这在利润公式中已经确定,因此完全有竞争力的公司可以以完全相同的价格出售任何数量的单位. 这意味着公司对其产品面临一个完全弹性的需求曲线:买方愿意以市场价格从公司购买任何数量的产出单位。 如果完全有竞争力的公司选择生产的数量,那么,这一数量 -- -- 与产出和投入市场的价格一道 -- -- 将决定公司的总收入、总成本以及最终的利润水平。

p39.original: Determining the Highest Profit by Comparing Total Revenue and Total Cost
p39.zh: 通过对比收入总额和费用总额确定最高利润

p40.original: A perfectly competitive firm can sell as large a quantity as it wishes, as long as it accepts the prevailing market price. The formula above shows that total revenue depends on the quantity sold and the price charged.  If the firm sells a higher quantity of output, then total revenue will increase. If the market price of the product increases, then total revenue also increases whatever the quantity of output sold. As an example of how a perfectly competitive firm decides what quantity to produce, consider the case of a small farmer who produces raspberries and sells them frozen for $4 per pack. Sales of one pack of raspberries will bring in $4, two packs will be $8, three packs will be $12, and so on. If, for example, the price of frozen raspberries doubles to $8 per pack, then sales of one pack of raspberries will be $8, two packs will be $16, three packs will be $24, and so on.
p40.zh: 完全具有竞争力的公司只要接受市场价格,就可以按自己的意愿销售数量。 上述公式表明,总收入取决于销售数量和收取的价格。 如果企业销售的产出数量较高,那么总收入就会增加. 如果产品市场价格上升,那么无论销售的产出数量如何,总收入也都会增加。 例如,一个完全具有竞争力的公司如何决定生产的数量,考虑到一个小农场主生产树莓并将其冷冻成每包4美元的价格。销售一包树莓能带来4元,两包8元,三包12元,等等. 例如,如果冰冻的树莓的价格是每包8美元翻倍,那么一包树莓的售价是8美元,两包16美元,三包24美元,等等.

p100.original: Based on its total revenue and total cost curves, a perfectly competitive firm like the raspberry farm can calculate the quantity of output that will provide the highest level of profit. At any given quantity, total revenue minus total cost will equal profit. One way to determine the most profitable quantity to produce is to see at what quantity total revenue exceeds total cost by the largest amount.  shows total revenue, total cost and profit using the data from .  The vertical gap between total revenue and total cost is profit, for example, at Q = 60, TR = 240 and TC = 165.  The difference is 75, which is the height of the profit curve at that output level. The firm doesn’t make a profit at every level of output. In this example, total costs will exceed total revenues at output levels from 0 to approximately 30, and so over this range of output, the firm will be making losses. At output levels from 40 to 100, total revenues exceed total costs, so the firm is earning profits. However, at any output greater than 100, total costs again exceed total revenues and the firm is making increasing losses. Total profits appear in the final column of . Maximum profit occurs at an output between 70 and 80, when profit equals $90.
p100.zh: 根据其总收入和总成本曲线,像树莓农场这样的完全具有竞争力的公司可以计算出能够提供最高利润水平的产出数量.任何特定数量的收入总额减去总成本后,都将等于利润。确定最有利可图的产量的一种方法是,用最大数额来判断总收入超过总成本的数量。总收入与总成本之间的垂直差距是利润,例如,Q=60,TR=240,TC=165.差值为75,是该产出水平的利润曲线的高度.公司并不在每个产出级别盈利。 在这个例子中,总成本将在产出水平上从0到约30之间超过总收入,因此,在产出范围上,公司将产生损失。 在40到100的产量水平上,总收入超过总成本,因此公司正在赚取利润. 然而,如果总产出超过100,总成本就再次超过总收入,而且公司的损失也在增加。利润总额列于.的最后一栏。最大利润发生在70至80之间的产出,而利润等于90美元。

p101.original: A higher price would mean that total revenue would be higher for every quantity sold. A lower price would mean that total revenue would be lower for every quantity sold. What happens if the price drops low enough so that the total revenue line is completely below the total cost curve; that is, at every level of output, total costs are higher than total revenues? In this instance, the best the firm can do is to suffer losses. However, a profit-maximizing firm will prefer the quantity of output where total revenues come closest to total costs and thus where the losses are smallest.
p101.zh: 较高的价格将意味着每一销售量的总收入都会更高。价格降低将意味着每一销售量的总收入都较低。 如果物价下跌幅度足够低,使总收入项目完全低于总成本曲线,也就是说,在每个产出层次,总成本都高于总收入,怎么办? 在这种情况下,公司所能做的最好就是遭受损失。 然而,利润最大化的公司更倾向于产出数量,如果总收入接近总成本,因而损失最小。

p103.original: Comparing Marginal Revenue and Marginal Costs
p103.zh: 比较边际收入和边际费用

p104.original: The approach that we described in the previous section, using total revenue and total cost, is not the only approach to determining the profit maximizing level of output.  In this section, we provide an alternative approach which uses marginal revenue and marginal cost.
p104.zh: 我们在上一节中描述的方法,使用总收入和总成本,并不是确定利润最大化产出水平的唯一方法. 在本节中,我们提供了一种使用边际收入和边际成本的替代办法。

p105.original: Firms often do not have the necessary data they need to draw a complete total cost curve for all levels of production. They cannot be sure of what total costs would look like if they, say, doubled production or cut production in half, because they have not tried it. Instead, firms experiment. They produce a slightly greater or lower quantity and observe how it affects profits. In economic terms, this practical approach to maximizing profits means examining how changes in production affect marginal revenue and marginal cost.
p105.zh: 公司往往没有为各级生产绘制完整的总成本曲线所需的必要数据。 他们不能确定,如果他们,比如说,将产量翻一番或将产量减半,那么总成本会是什么样子,因为他们没有尝试过。 相反,公司进行实验。 它们生产的数量略高或略低,并观察它如何影响利润。 在经济方面,这种实现利润最大化的实用方法意味着审查生产变化如何影响边际收入和边际成本.

As mentioned before, a firm in perfect competition faces a perfectly elastic demand curve for its product—that is, the firm’s demand curve is a horizontal line drawn at the market price level. This also means that the firm’s marginal revenue curve is the same as the firm’s demand curve: Every time a consumer demands one more unit, the firm sells one more unit and revenue increases by exactly the same amount equal to the market price. In this example, every time the firm sells a pack of frozen raspberries, the firm’s revenue increases by $4.  shows an example of this. p130.original: Ordinarily, marginal cost changes as the firm produces a greater quantity.
p130.zh: 通常,随着公司生产的数量增加,边际成本会发生变化。

p131.original: In the raspberry farm example, in  and , marginal cost at first declines as production increases from 10 to 20 to 30 to 40 packs of raspberries—which represents the area of increasing marginal returns that is not uncommon at low levels of production. At some point, though, marginal costs start to increase, displaying the typical pattern of diminishing marginal returns. If the firm is producing at a quantity where MR > MC, like 40 or 50 packs of raspberries, then it can increase profit by increasing output because the marginal revenue is exceeding the marginal cost. If the firm is producing at a quantity where MC > MR, like 90 or 100 packs, then it can increase profit by reducing output because the reductions in marginal cost will exceed the reductions in marginal revenue. The firm’s profit-maximizing choice of output will occur where MR = MC (or at a choice close to that point).
p131.zh: 在树莓农场的例子中,随着产量从10袋树莓增加到20袋,其边际成本起初会下降至30至40袋树莓,这意味着在低生产水平下边际回报率不断上升。 然而,在某个时候,边际成本开始增加,显示了边际回报不断减少的典型模式. 如果公司生产的数量是MR > MC,如40或50包树莓,那么它可以通过增加产出来增加利润,因为边际收入超过边际成本。 如果公司生产的数量是MC > MR, 如90或100包,那么它可以通过减少产出来增加利润,因为边际成本的减少将超过边际收入的减少。公司在MR = MC(或选择接近于这个点)的情况下,将进行利润最大化的产出选择。

p219.original: In this example, the marginal revenue and marginal cost curves cross at a price of $4 and a quantity of 80 produced. If the farmer started out producing at a level of 60, and then experimented with increasing production to 70, marginal revenues from the increase in production would exceed marginal costs—and so profits would rise. The farmer has an incentive to keep producing. At a level of output of 80, marginal cost and marginal revenue are equal so profit doesn’t change. If the farmer then experimented further with increasing production from 80 to 90, he would find that marginal costs from the increase in production are greater than marginal revenues, and so profits would decline.
p219.zh: 在这个例子中,边际收入和边际成本曲线以4美元的价格交叉,生产的数量为80美元。 如果农民开始生产达到60级,然后试验将生产增加到70级,那么生产增加带来的边际收入将超过边际成本——因此利润会增加。农民有继续生产的积极性. 在80个产出水平上,边际成本和边际收入是相等的,因此利润不会改变。 如果农民随后进一步试验将产量从80提高到90,他就会发现生产增长带来的边际成本大于边际收入,因此利润会下降.

p220.original: The profit-maximizing choice for a perfectly competitive firm will occur at the level of output where marginal revenue is equal to marginal cost—that is, where MR = MC. This occurs at Q = 80 in the figure.
p220.zh: 完全具有竞争力的公司利润最大化的选择将发生在产出水平上,其中边际收入等于边际成本,即MR=MC。 这发生在Q=80的数值。

p221.original: Does Profit Maximization Occur at a Range of Output or a Specific Level of Output?
p221.zh: 最大利润是否出现在输出范围或特定输出水平上?

p222.original: Because the marginal revenue received by a perfectly competitive firm is equal to the price P, we can also write the profit-maximizing rule for a perfectly competitive firm as a recommendation to produce at the quantity of output where P = MC.
p222.zh: 由于完全有竞争力的公司获得的边际收入与P的价格相等,我们也可以将完全有竞争力的公司利润最大化规则写成建议在P=MC的输出数量中生产。

p223.original: Profits and Losses with the Average Cost Curve
p223.zh: 平均成本曲线的利润和损失

p224.original: Does maximizing profit (producing where MR = MC) imply an actual economic profit? The answer depends on the relationship between price and average total cost, which is the average profit or profit margin. If the market price is higher than the firm's average cost of production for that quantity produced, then the profit margin is positive and the firm will earn profits. Conversely, if the market price is lower than the  average cost of production, the profit margin is negative and the firm will suffer losses. You might think that, in this situation, the firm may want to shut down immediately. Remember, however, that the firm has already paid for fixed costs, such as equipment, so it may continue to produce for a while and incur a loss.  continues the raspberry farm example.  illustrates the three possible scenarios: (a) where price intersects marginal cost at a level above the average cost curve, (b) where price intersects marginal cost at a level equal to the average cost curve, and (c) where price intersects marginal cost at a level below the average cost curve.
p224.zh: 利润最大化(在MR = MC 生产时)是否意味着实际经济利润?答案取决于价格与平均总成本之间的关系,即平均利润率或利润率. 如果市场价格高于公司生产该数量的平均生产成本,则利润率为正值,公司将赚取利润。 相反,如果市场价格低于平均生产成本,则利润率为负值,公司将遭受损失。 你可能会认为,在这种情况下,公司可能想 立即关闭。 但是,要记住,公司已经支付了设备等固定费用,因此可以继续生产一段时间,并蒙受损失。

p226.original: First consider a situation where the price is equal to $5 for a pack of frozen raspberries. Remember that the area of a rectangle is equal to its base multiplied by its height. The farm’s total revenue at this price will be shown by the rectangle from the origin over to a quantity of 85 packs (the base) up to point E' (the height), over to the price of $5, and back to the origin. The difference between total revenues and total costs is profits. Thus, profits will be the blue shaded rectangle on top.

p235.original: If the market price that perfectly competitive firm receives leads it to produce at a quantity where the price is greater than average cost, the firm will earn profits. If the price the firm receives causes it to produce at a quantity where price equals average cost, which occurs at the minimum point of the AC curve, then the firm earns zero profits. Finally, if the price the firm receives leads it to produce at a quantity where the price is less than average cost, the firm will earn losses.  summarizes this.
p235.zh: 如果完全具有竞争力的公司得到的市场价格导致其生产的数量大于平均成本,公司将赚取利润。 如果公司收到的价格导致其生产的数量相当于平均成本,而平均成本发生在AC曲线最小点,则公司赚取的利润为零。 最后,如果公司收到的价格导致它以低于平均成本的数量生产,公司将赚取损失。

p244.original: Which intersection should a firm choose?
p244.zh: 一个公司应该选择哪一个交叉点?

p245.original: At a price of $2, MR intersects MC at two points: Q = 20 and Q = 65.  It never makes sense for a firm to choose a level of output on the downward sloping part of the MC curve, because the profit is lower (the loss is bigger). Thus, the correct choice of output is Q = 65.
p245.zh: 以2美元的价格,MR在两个点上与MC相交:Q=20,Q=65.公司在MC曲线向下倾斜的部分上选择产出水平是没有道理的,因为利润较低(损失更大). 因此,产出的正确选择是Q=65.

p247.original: The possibility that a firm may earn losses raises a question: Why can the firm not avoid losses by shutting down and not producing at all? The answer is that shutting down can reduce variable costs to zero, but in the short run, the firm has already paid for fixed costs. As a result, if the firm produces a quantity of zero, it would still make losses because it would still need to pay for its fixed costs. Therefore when a firm is experiencing losses, it must face a question: should it continue producing or should it shut down?
p247.zh: 公司可能获得损失的可能性提出了一个问题:公司为什么不能通过关闭和完全不生产而避免损失?答案是,关闭可以将可变成本降低到零,但在短期内,公司已经支付了固定成本. 因此,如果该公司生产的数量为零,它仍然会蒙受损失,因为它仍然需要支付其固定费用。 因此,当一家公司正在遭受损失时,它必须面对一个问题:它应该继续生产还是应该关闭?

p248.original: As an example, consider the situation of the Yoga Center, which has signed a contract to rent space that costs $10,000 per month. If the firm decides to operate, its marginal costs for hiring yoga teachers is $15,000 for the month. If the firm shuts down, it must still pay the rent, but it would not need to hire labor.  shows three possible scenarios. In the first scenario, the Yoga Center does not have any clients, and therefore does not make any revenues, in which case it faces losses of $10,000 equal to the fixed costs. In the second scenario, the Yoga Center has clients that earn the center revenues of $10,000 for the month, but ultimately experiences losses of $15,000 due to having to hire yoga instructors to cover the classes. In the third scenario, the Yoga Center earns revenues of $20,000 for the month, but experiences losses of $5,000.
p248.zh: 例如,考虑瑜伽中心的情况,该中心已经签署了每月费用为10 000美元的租赁空间合同。 如果公司决定经营,其雇用瑜伽教师的边际费用为每月15,000美元。 如果公司倒闭,它仍必须支付租金,但它不需要雇用劳动力。 第一种情况是,瑜伽中心没有任何客户,因此不产生任何收入,在这种情况下,它面临相当于固定成本的10 000美元的损失。 在第二种情况下,瑜伽中心的客户本月收入为10,000美元,但最终因不得不聘请瑜伽教官来承担课时而损失15,000美元. 在第三种情况中,瑜伽中心当月的收入为2万美元,但经历了5000美元的损失.

p249.original: In all three cases, the Yoga Center loses money. In all three cases, when the rental contract expires in the long run, assuming revenues do not improve, the firm should exit this business. In the short run, though, the decision varies depending on the level of losses and whether the firm can cover its variable costs. In scenario 1, the center does not have any revenues, so hiring yoga teachers would increase variable costs and losses, so it should shut down and only incur its fixed costs. In scenario 2, the center’s losses are greater because it does not make enough revenue to offset the increased variable costs, so it should shut down immediately and only incur its fixed costs. If price is below the minimum average variable cost, the firm must shut down. In contrast, in scenario 3 the revenue that the center can earn is high enough that the losses diminish when it remains open, so the center should remain open in the short run.
p249.zh: 三例中,瑜伽中心亏损.在所有三种情况下,如果长期租金合同到期,假定收入没有改善,公司应退出这一业务。 不过,在短期内,决定的差别取决于损失的程度以及公司是否能够支付其可变费用。 在情景1中,中心没有任何收入,因此聘请瑜伽教师会增加可变成本和损失,因此它应该关闭,只承担固定成本. 在情景2中,中心的损失更大,因为它没有足够的收入来抵消增加的可变费用,因此应当立即关闭,只承担固定费用。 如果价格低于最低平均可变成本,公司必须关闭。与此相反,在情景3中,中心能够赚取的收入足够高,损失在保持开放时会减少,因此中心在短期内应该保持开放.

When the firm is operating below the break-even point, where price equals average cost, it is operating at a loss so it faces two options: continue to produce and lose money or shutdown.  Which option is preferable?  The one that loses the least money is the best choice.
p260.zh: 说明以下教训,即保持开放要求价格超过公司的平均可变成本。 当公司在价格等于平均成本的断面点以下运作时,它就亏损地运作,因此它面临两种选择:继续生产并损失资金或关闭。 哪一种选择更可取?输钱最少的就是最好的选择

p261.original: At a price of $2.00 per pack, as Figure 8.6 (a) illustrates, if the farm stays in operation it will produce at a level of 65 packs of raspberries, and it will make losses of $47.45 (as explained earlier).  The alternative would be to shut down and lose all the fixed costs of $62.00.  Since losing $47.45 is preferable to losing $62.00, the profit maximizing (or in this case the loss minimizing) choice is to stay in operation.  The key reason is because price is above average variable cost.  This means that at the current price the farm can pay all its variable costs, and have some revenue left over to pay some of the fixed costs.  So the loss represents the part of the fixed costs the farm can’t pay, which is less than the entire fixed costs. However, if the price declined to $1.50 per pack, as  (b) shows, and if the firm applied its rule of producing where P = MR = MC, it would produce a quantity of 60. This price is below average variable cost for this level of output. If the farmer cannot pay workers (the variable costs), then it has to shut down. At this price and output, total revenues would be $90 (quantity of 60 times price of $1.50) and total cost would be $165, for overall losses of $75. If the farm shuts down, it must pay only its fixed costs of $62, so shutting down is preferable to selling at a price of $1.50 per pack.
p261.zh: 如图8.6(a)所示,每包价格为2.00美元,如果农场继续经营,将生产65包树莓,损失47.45美元(如前所述)。另一种办法是关闭并损失所有固定费用62美元。 由于损失47.45美元比损失62.00美元更好,利润最大化(或在此情况下,损失最小)的选择是保持运行.主要原因是价格高于平均可变成本。 这意味着,按现时价格,农场可以支付所有可变成本,并拥有一些收入来支付某些固定成本。损失是农场无法支付的部分固定成本, 但是,如果价格下降到每包1.50美元,如(b)所示,如果公司适用其生产P = MR = MC 的规则,则其生产量将达到60美元。 这一价格低于这一产出水平的平均可变成本。 如果农民无力支付工人工资(可变成本),则必须关闭。 按这一价格和产出计算,总收入为90美元(为价格的60倍,即1.50美元),总费用为165美元,总损失为75美元。 如果农场停业,它必须只支付固定的62美元费用,因此停业比每包1.50美元的价格要好。

p321.original:
The intersection of the average variable cost curve and the marginal cost curve, which shows the price below which the firm would lack enough revenue to cover its variable costs, is called the shutdown point. If the perfectly competitive firm faces a market price above the shutdown point, then the firm is at least covering its average variable costs. At a price above the shutdown point, the firm  is also making enough revenue to cover at least a portion of fixed costs, so it should limp ahead even if it is making losses in the short run, since at least those losses will be smaller than if the firm shuts down immediately and incurs a loss equal to total fixed costs. However, if the firm is receiving a price below the price at the shutdown point, then the firm is not even covering its variable costs. In this case, staying open is making the firm’s losses larger, and it should shut down immediately. To summarize, if:
   
price < minimum average variable cost, then firm shuts down
price > minimum average variable cost, then firm stays in business
p321.zh: 平均可变成本曲线与边际成本曲线的交汇点称为停产点,它显示公司在低于该价格时将缺乏足够的收入来支付其可变成本. 如果完全有竞争力的公司面临超过停产点的市场价格,那么该公司至少要支付其平均可变成本。 在超过停产点的价格下,该公司也正在创造足够的收入,至少能够支付一部分固定费用,因此即使短期内造成损失,该公司也应向前行驶,因为至少这些损失将比该公司立即停产并遭受相当于全部固定费用的损失要小。 但是,如果公司在停产点得到的价格低于价格,那么公司甚至无法支付其可变费用。 在这种情况下,保持开放使得公司的损失增加,它应立即关闭。概括而言,如果价格 < 最低平均可变成本,则公司关闭价格 > 最低平均可变成本,然后公司继续经营。

p323.original: The average cost and average variable cost curves divide the marginal cost curve into three segments, as  shows. At the market price, which the perfectly competitive firm accepts as given, the profit-maximizing firm chooses the output level where price or marginal revenue, which are the same thing for a perfectly competitive firm, is equal to marginal cost: P = MR = MC.

p325.original: First consider the upper zone, where prices are above the level where marginal cost (MC) crosses average cost (AC) at the zero profit point. At any price above that level, the firm will earn profits in the short run. If the price falls exactly on the break even point where the MC and AC curves cross, then the firm earns zero profits. If a price falls into the zone between the break even point, where MC crosses AC, and the shutdown point, where MC crosses AVC, the firm will be making losses in the short run—but since the firm is more than covering its variable costs, the losses are smaller than if the firm shut down immediately. Finally, consider a price at or below the shutdown point where MC crosses AVC. At any price like this one, the firm will shut down immediately, because it cannot even cover its variable costs.
p325.zh: 首先考虑上区,其价格高于边际成本(MC)在零利润点上超过平均成本(AC)的水平.任何高于这一水平的价格,公司都会在短期内赚取利润. 如果价格完全跌到中间点,甚至MC和AC曲线交叉点,那么公司就获得零利润。 如果在MC穿越AC的断面点和MC穿越AVC的关闭点之间,价格跌入区间,则公司在短期内将产生损失——但由于公司不止承担其可变成本,损失比公司立即关闭时要小。 最后,考虑在MC跨越AVC的关闭点或低于关闭点的价格。这样的公司无论以什么价格,都会立即关闭,因为它甚至无法支付其可变成本.

p326.original: Marginal Cost and the Firm’s Supply Curve
p326.zh: 边际成本和公司的供应曲线

p327.original: For a perfectly competitive firm, the marginal cost curve is identical to the firm’s supply curve starting from the minimum point on the average variable cost curve. To understand why this perhaps surprising insight holds true, first think about what the supply curve means. A firm checks the market price and then looks at its supply curve to decide what quantity to produce. Now, think about what it means to say that a firm will maximize its profits by producing at the quantity where P = MC. This rule means that the firm checks the market price, and then looks at its marginal cost to determine the quantity to produce—and makes sure that the price is greater than the minimum average variable cost. In other words, the marginal cost curve above the minimum point on the average variable cost curve becomes the firm’s supply curve.
p327.zh: 对于一个完全具有竞争力的公司,边际成本曲线与公司从平均可变成本曲线最低点开始的供应曲线相同。 要理解为什么这个也许令人惊讶的见解是真实的,首先要考虑一下供应曲线的含义。一家企业检查市场价格,然后查看其供应曲线,以确定生产的数量。 现在,想一想,这是什么意思 说一个公司将实现利润最大化 通过生产的数量 在P=MC。 这一规则意味着,公司要检查市场价格,然后考虑其边际成本,以确定生产的数量,并确保价格高于最低平均可变成本。换言之,平均可变成本曲线上最低点以上的边际成本曲线成为公司的供应曲线。

p329.original: As we discussed in the chapter on Demand and Supply, many of the reasons that supply curves shift relate to underlying changes in costs. For example, a lower price of key inputs or new technologies that reduce production costs cause supply to shift to the right. In contrast, bad weather or added government regulations can add to costs of certain goods in a way that causes supply to shift to the left. We can also interpret these shifts in the firm’s supply curve as shifts of the marginal cost curve. A shift in costs of production that increases marginal costs at all levels of output—and shifts MC upward and to the left—will cause a perfectly competitive firm to produce less at any given market price. Conversely, a shift in costs of production that decreases marginal costs at all levels of output will shift MC downward and to the right and as a result, a competitive firm will choose to expand its level of output at any given price. The following Work It Out feature will walk you through an example.
p329.zh: 正如我们在关于需求和供应的一章中所讨论的,供应曲线变化的许多原因都与成本的根本变化有关。 例如,降低生产成本的关键投入或新技术价格较低,导致供应转向右翼。与此相反,恶劣天气或增加政府规章可能会增加某些商品的成本,从而导致供应转向左侧。 我们还可将公司供应曲线的这些变动解释为边际成本曲线的变动。生产成本的变动会增加各级产出的边际成本——使MC向上和向左转移——将导致一个完全有竞争力的公司以任何特定市场价格减少生产。 相反,生产成本的转移,如果降低各级产出的边际成本,则MC就会向下和向右转变,因此,有竞争力的公司将选择以任何特定价格扩大其产出水平。 下面的“工作它”功能会带你们通过一个实例。

p586.original: As a perfectly competitive firm produces a greater quantity of output, its total revenue steadily increases at a constant rate determined by the given market price. Profits will be highest (or losses will be smallest) at the quantity of output where total revenues exceed total costs by the greatest amount (or where total revenues fall short of total costs by the smallest amount). Alternatively, profits will be highest where marginal revenue, which is price for a perfectly competitive firm, is equal to marginal cost. If the market price faced by a perfectly competitive firm is above average cost at the profit-maximizing quantity of output, then the firm is making profits. If the market price is below average cost at the profit-maximizing quantity of output, then the firm is making losses.
p586.zh: 作为一个完全具有竞争力的公司,其产出数量较多,其总收入以一定市场价格确定的恒定速率稳步增长。利润最高(或损失最小)的,按产出数量计算,如果收入总额超过总费用,则最高(或总收入低于总费用,则最低)。 或者,如果边缘收入,即完全具有竞争力的公司的价格,等于边际成本,利润就会最高。 如果完全有竞争力的公司所面临的市场价格高于平均成本,而产出的利润最大化,则该公司正在盈利。 如果市场价格低于平均成本,而产出的利润最大化数量,则公司正在产生损失。

p587.original: If the market price is equal to average cost at the profit-maximizing level of output, then the firm is making zero profits. We call the point where the marginal cost curve crosses the average cost curve, at the minimum of the average cost curve, the “zero profit point.” If the market price that a perfectly competitive firm faces is below average variable cost at the profit-maximizing quantity of output, then the firm should shut down operations immediately. If the market price that a perfectly competitive firm faces is above average variable cost, but below average cost, then the firm should continue producing in the short run, but exit in the long run. We call the point where the marginal cost curve crosses the average variable cost curve the shutdown point.
p587.zh: 如果市场价格等于按利润最大化的产出水平的平均成本,那么公司正在取得零利润. 我们把边际成本曲线越过平均成本曲线的点称为“零利润点 ” 。 如果完全有竞争力的公司面值的市场价格低于平均可变成本,而产出数量达到利润最大化,那么公司就应立即关闭业务。 如果一个完全具有竞争力的公司所面临的市场价格高于平均可变成本,但低于平均成本,那么公司就应该在短期内继续生产,但长期退出。 我们把边际成本曲线越过平均可变成本曲线的点称为关闭点。

p768.zh: AAA水族馆股份有限公司出售水族馆,每家售价20元.固定生产成本为20元. 一个水族馆的总可变费用为20美元,两个单元25美元,三个单元35美元,四个单元50美元,五个单元80美元。以表格形式计算每个产出水平(一至五个单位)的总收入,边际收入,总成本,边际成本.产出的利润最大化数量是多少?在一个图上,勾画总收入和总成本曲线. 在另一个图中,勾画边际收入和边际成本曲线.

p769.original: Perfectly competitive firm Doggies Paradise Inc. sells winter coats for dogs. Dog coats sell for $72 each. The fixed costs of production are $100. The total variable costs are $64 for one unit, $84 for two units, $114 for three units, $184 for four units, and $270 for five units. p769.zh: 竞争激烈的Doggies Paradise Inc. 出售冬季外套给狗.狗衣每件售价72元.固定生产成本为100元. 一个单位的可变费用总额为64美元,两个单位84美元,三个单位114美元,四个单位184美元,五个单位270美元。以表格形式计算每个产出级别(一至五个单位)的总收入,边际收入,总成本和边际成本.在一个图上,勾画总收入和总成本曲线. 在另一个图中,勾画边际收入和边际成本曲线.最大利润的数量是多少?

p771.original: Entry and Exit Decisions in the Long Run

p772.original: It is impossible to precisely define the line between the short run and the long run with a stopwatch, or even with a calendar. It varies according to the specific business. Therefore, the distinction between the short run and the long run is  more technical: in the short run, firms cannot change the usage of fixed inputs, while in the long run, the firm can adjust all factors of production.
p772.zh: 无法用停表,甚至用日历精确地定义短跑和长跑之间的界线. 它因具体业务的不同而不同. 因此,短期与长期之间的区别比较技术性:从短期来看,公司不能改变固定投入的用途,而从长期来看,公司可以调整所有生产要素.

p773.original: In a competitive market, profits are a red cape that incites businesses to charge. If a business is making a profit in the short run, it has an incentive to expand existing factories or to build new ones. New firms may start production, as well. When new firms enter the industry in response to increased industry profits it is called entry.
p773.zh: 在竞争性市场中,利润是一种红色披风,会煽动企业收费. 如果一个企业在短期内正在盈利,那么它就有了扩大现有工厂或建造新工厂的动机.新的公司也可能开始生产。 当新公司因工业利润增加而进入该行业时,就称为进入。

p774.original: Losses are the black thundercloud that causes businesses to flee. If a business is making losses in the short run, it will either keep limping along or just shut down, depending on whether its revenues are covering its variable costs. But in the long run, firms that are facing losses will cease production altogether. The long-run process of reducing production in response to a sustained pattern of losses is called exit. The following Clear It Up feature discusses where some of these losses might come from, and the reasons why some firms go out of business.
p774.zh: 损失是导致企业逃亡的黑雷云. 如果一个企业在短期内出现亏损,那么它要么继续停滞不前,要么干脆停业,这取决于其收入是否弥补了其可变成本。 但从长远来看,面临损失的公司将完全停止生产。为应对持续亏损模式而减少生产的长期过程称为退出. 以下的Clear Up 特征讨论了其中一些损失可能来自何处,以及一些公司退出业务的原因。

p775.original: Why do firms cease to exist?

p776.original: Can we say anything about what causes a firm to exit an industry? Profits are the measurement that determines whether a business stays operating or not. Individuals start businesses with the purpose of making profits. They invest their money, time, effort, and many other resources to produce and sell something that they hope will give them something in return. Unfortunately, not all businesses are successful, and many new startups soon realize that their “business venture” must eventually end.
p776.zh: 我们能说说是什么导致公司退出行业吗?利润是决定企业是否继续经营的衡量标准。个人以盈利为目的创业. 他们投入他们的钱、时间、精力和许多其他资源来生产和销售他们希望能够给他们一些回报的东西。 不幸的是,并非所有的企业都成功,许多新的创业企业很快意识到,他们的“商业风险”必须最终结束。

p777.original: In the model of perfectly competitive firms, those that consistently cannot make money will “exit,” which is a nice, bloodless word for a more painful process. When a business fails, after all, workers lose their jobs, investors lose their money, and owners and managers can lose their dreams. Many businesses fail. The U.S. Small Business Administration indicates that in 2011, 534,907 new firms "entered," and 575,691 firms failed.
p777.zh: 在完全有竞争力的公司模式中,那些一贯无法赚钱的公司将“退出”,这是一个更痛苦的过程的好、无血的词。 当一个企业失败时,毕竟工人失业,投资者失去钱财,所有者和管理人员可能失去梦想. 许多企业都失败了。 美国.小企业管理局表示,2011年,534,907家新公司"进入",575,691家公司失败.

p778.original: Sometimes a business fails because of poor management or workers who are not very productive, or because of tough domestic or foreign competition. Businesses also fail from a variety of causes. For example, conditions of demand and supply in the market may shift in an unexpected way, so that the prices that a business charges for outputs fall or the prices for inputs rise. With millions of businesses in the U.S. economy, even a small fraction of them failing will affect many people—and business failures can be very hard on the workers and managers directly involved. However, from the standpoint of the overall economic system, business exits are sometimes a necessary evil if a market-oriented system is going to offer a flexible mechanism for satisfying customers, keeping costs low, and inventing new products.
p778.zh: 有时,由于管理不善或工人生产效率不高,或由于国内或国外竞争激烈,企业失败。企业也因为各种原因失败. 例如,市场供求条件可能以出乎意料的方式发生变化,从而导致产出的商业收费价格下降或投入价格上升。 美国经济有数百万家企业,即使其中一小部分企业倒闭也会影响到许多人——而企业倒闭对直接涉及的工人和管理人员来说可能非常困难. 然而,从整个经济体制的角度来看,如果面向市场的制度能够提供一种灵活的机制,满足客户的需求,降低成本,发明新产品,则商业退出有时是必然的邪恶。

p779.original: How Entry and Exit Lead to Zero Profits in the Long Run
p779.zh: 进出境如何在长跑中导致零利润

p780.original: No perfectly competitive firm acting alone can affect the market price. However, the combination of many firms entering or exiting the market will affect overall supply in the market. In turn, a shift in supply for the market as a whole will affect the market price. Entry and exit to and from the market are the driving forces behind a process that, in the long run, pushes the price down to minimum average total costs so that all firms are earning a zero profit.
p780.zh: 任何完全有竞争力的公司单独行动都无法影响市场价格。 然而,许多公司进出市场的组合将影响市场的总体供应。反过来,整个市场供应的转变将影响市场价格。 从长远来看,将价格推到最低平均总成本,使所有公司都获得零利润。 进入和退出市场是这一进程的驱动力。

p781.original: To understand how short-run profits for a perfectly competitive firm will evaporate in the long run, imagine the following situation. The market is in long-run equilibrium, where all firms earn zero economic profits producing the output level where P = MR = MC and P = AC. No firm has the incentive to enter or leave the market. Let’s say that the product’s demand increases, and with that, the market price goes up. The existing firms in the industry are now facing a higher price than before, so they will increase production to the new output level where P = MR = MC.
p781.zh: 要了解完全具有竞争力的公司短期利润从长远来看会如何蒸发,想象下的情况.市场处于长期平衡状态,所有公司都从中赚取零经济利润,产出水平为P=MR=MC,P=AC。任何企业都不得有进入或离开市场的动机。 让我们假设产品的需求会增加, 市场价格也会随之上涨。 该行业现有公司现在面临比以前更高的价格,因此它们将把产量提高到P=MR=MC的新产出水平。

p782.original: This will temporarily make the market price rise above the minimum point on the average cost curve, and therefore, the existing firms in the market will now be earning economic profits. However, these economic profits attract other firms to enter the market. Entry of many new firms causes the market supply curve to shift to the right. As the supply curve shifts to the right, the market price starts decreasing, and with that, economic profits fall for new and existing firms. As long as there are still profits in the market, entry will continue to shift supply to the right. This will stop whenever the market price is driven down to the zero-profit level, where no firm is earning economic profits.
p782.zh: 这将暂时使市场价格高于平均成本曲线的最低点,因此,市场上现有公司现在将赚取经济利润。 然而,这些经济利润吸引了其他公司进入市场。 许多新公司的进入导致市场供应曲线向右转变。 随着供应曲线向右转,市场价格开始下降,因此,新公司和现有公司的经济利润下降。 只要市场仍有利润,进入将继续将供应转向右翼. 只要市场价格降到零利润水平,而没有任何公司在赚取经济利润,这种情况就会停止。

p783.original: Short-run losses will fade away by reversing this process. Say that the market is in long-run equilibrium. This time, instead, demand decreases, and with that, the market price starts falling. The existing firms in the industry are now facing a lower price than before, and as it will be below the average cost curve, they will now be making economic losses. Some firms will continue producing where the new P = MR = MC, as long as they are able to cover their average variable costs. Some firms will have to shut down immediately as they will not be able to cover their average variable costs, and will then only incur their fixed costs, minimizing their losses. Exit of many firms causes the market supply curve to shift to the left. As the supply curve shifts to the left, the market price starts rising, and economic losses start to be lower. This process ends whenever the market price rises to the zero-profit level, where the existing firms are no longer losing money and are at zero profits again. Thus, while a perfectly competitive firm can earn profits in the short run, in the long run the process of entry will push down prices until they reach the zero-profit level. Conversely, while a perfectly competitive firm may earn losses in the short run, firms will not continually lose money. In the long run, firms making losses are able to escape from their fixed costs, and their exit from the market will push the price back up to the zero-profit level. In the long run, this process of entry and exit will drive the price in perfectly competitive markets to the zero-profit point at the bottom of the AC curve, where marginal cost crosses average cost.
p783.zh: 短期损失将通过扭转这一进程而消失。说市场处于长期均衡状态. 这次,需求反而减少,随着这一次,市场价格开始下跌。 该行业现有公司现在面临比以前更低的价格,由于价格将低于平均成本曲线,它们现在将蒙受经济损失。 有些公司将继续生产新的P=MR=MC,只要它们能够支付平均可变成本。 有些公司将不得不立即关闭,因为它们将无法支付其平均可变费用,因此只能承担其固定费用,尽量减少其损失。 许多公司退出,导致市场供应曲线向左转移。 随着供给曲线向左转,市场价格开始上涨,经济损失开始降低. 只要市场价格上升至零利润水平,而现有公司不再失去资金,再次处于零利润状态,这一进程就会结束。 因此,虽然一个完全有竞争力的公司在短期内能够赚取利润,但从长远来看,进入过程将推低价格,直至达到零利润水平。 相反,虽然一个完全具有竞争力的公司在短期内可能亏损,但公司不会持续亏损。 从长远来看,亏损企业能够摆脱固定成本,退出市场将推动价格回升至零盈利水平. 从长远来看,这种进出境过程将推动在完全竞争的市场上的价格到AC曲线下方的零利润点,其中边际成本跨越平均成本.

p784.original: The Long-Run Adjustment and Industry Types

p785.original: Whenever there are expansions in an industry, costs of production for the existing and new firms could either stay the same, increase, or even decrease. Therefore, we can categorize an industry as being (1) a constant-cost industry (as demand increases, the cost of production for firms stays the same), (2) an increasing-cost industry (as demand increases, the cost of production for firms increases), or (3) a decreasing-cost industry (as demand increases the costs of production for the firms decreases).
p785.zh: 只要某一行业出现扩张,现有和新公司的生产成本就可能保持不变、增加甚至减少。 因此,我们可以将一个工业归类为:(1) 恒定成本工业(随着需求增加,公司生产成本保持不变),(2) 成本增加的工业(随着需求增加,公司生产成本增加),或(3) 成本降低的工业(随着需求增加,公司生产成本下降)。

p786.original: For a constant-cost industry, whenever there is an increase in market demand and price, then the supply curve shifts to the right with new firms’ entry and stops at the point where the new long-run equilibrium intersects at the same market price as before. This is the case of constant returns to scale, which we discussed earlier in the chapter on Production, Costs, and Industry Structure. However, why will costs remain the same? In this type of industry, the supply curve is very elastic. Firms can easily supply any quantity that consumers demand. In addition, there is a perfectly elastic supply of inputs—firms can easily increase their demand for employees, for example, with no increase to wages. Tying in to our Bring it Home discussion, an increased demand for ethanol in recent years has caused the demand for corn to increase. Consequently, many farmers switched from growing wheat to growing corn. Agricultural markets are generally good examples of constant-cost industries.
p786.zh: 对于一个不断成本的产业,每当市场需求和价格增加时,供应曲线随新公司的进入而向右转,并在新的长期平衡以与以前相同的市场价格交叉时止步。 这就是我们先前在关于生产、成本和工业结构的一章中讨论的不断恢复规模的情况。 但是,为什么费用保持不变? 在这类工业中,供给曲线具有很强的弹性.公司可以很容易地供应消费者需要的任何数量。 此外,投入的供应具有完全的弹性——公司很容易增加其对雇员的需求,例如,工资没有增加。与我们回家的讨论挂钩的是,近年来对乙醇的需求增加,导致对玉米的需求增加。 因此,许多农民从种植小麦转向种植玉米。农业市场一般是不断成本的工业的良好例子。

p787.original: For an increasing-cost industry, as the market expands, the old and new firms experience increases in their costs of production, which makes the new zero-profit level intersect at a higher price than before. Here companies may have to deal with limited inputs, such as skilled labor. As the demand for these workers rises, wages rise and this increases the cost of production for all firms. The industry supply curve in this type of industry is more inelastic.
p787.zh: 对于成本不断上升的工业,随着市场扩张,新老企业的生产成本不断上涨,使得新的零利润水平以比以前更高的价格交叉. 在这方面,公司可能不得不处理有限的投入,如熟练劳动力。 随着对这些工人需求的增加,工资增加,这增加了所有企业的生产成本。 这类工业的工业供应曲线更具弹性.

p788.original: For a decreasing-cost industry, as the market expands, the old and new firms experience lower costs of production, which makes the new zero-profit level intersect at a lower price than before. In this case, the industry and all the firms in it are experiencing falling average total costs. This can be due to an improvement in technology in the entire industry or an increase in the education of employees. High-tech industries may be a good example of a decreasing-cost market.
p788.zh: 对于一个成本不断下降的产业,随着市场扩张,新老企业的生产成本降低,使得新的零利润水平以比以前更低的价格交叉. 在这种情况下,该行业及其所有公司的平均总成本正在下降。这可能是由于整个行业的技术改进或雇员教育的增加.高技术工业可能是成本下降市场的一个良好例子。

p789.original: (a) presents the case of an adjustment process in a constant-cost industry. Whenever there are output expansions in this type of industry, the long-run outcome implies more output produced at exactly the same original price. Note that supply was able to increase to meet the increased demand. When we join the before and after long-run equilibriums, the resulting line is the long run supply (LRS) curve in perfectly competitive markets. In this case, it is a flat curve.  (b) and  (c) present the cases for an increasing-cost and decreasing-cost industry, respectively. For an increasing-cost industry, the LRS is upward sloping, while for a decreasing-cost industry, the LRS is downward sloping.
p789.zh: (a) 介绍一个经常成本行业的调整过程。每当这类工业出现产出扩张时,长期结果意味着以完全相同的原始价格生产更多的产出。请注意,供应量能够增加,以满足增加的需求。 当我们加入长期平衡之前和之后,由此产生的线是完全竞争性市场中的长期供应曲线。 在这种情况下,它是一个平坦的曲线。(b)和(c)分别说明成本上升和成本下降的行业的情况。 对于成本不断上升的工业来说,LRS向上倾斜,而对于成本不断下降的工业来说,LRS向下倾斜。

p790.original: Adjustment Process in a Constant-Cost Industry
p790.zh: 固定成本行业的调整程序

p792.original: In the long run, firms will respond to profits through a process of entry, where existing firms expand output and new firms enter the market. Conversely, firms will react to losses in the long run through a process of exit, in which existing firms cease production altogether. Through the process of entry in response to profits and exit in response to losses, the price level in a perfectly competitive market will move toward the zero-profit point, where the marginal cost curve crosses the AC curve at the minimum of the average cost curve.
p792.zh: 从长远来看,公司将通过一个进入过程来应对利润,即现有公司扩大产出,新公司进入市场。 相反,从长远来看,公司将通过退出过程对损失作出反应,在退出过程中,现有公司完全停止生产。 通过针对利润的输入过程和针对损失的退出过程,一个完全竞争的市场中的价格水平将走向零利润点,边际成本曲线在平均成本曲线的最小范围内跨越AC曲线.

p793.original: The long-run supply curve shows the long-run output supplied by firms in three different types of industries: constant cost, increasing cost, and decreasing cost.
p793.zh: 长期供应曲线显示三个不同行业的公司提供的长期产出:持续成本、成本增加和成本下降。

p795.original: If new technology in a perfectly competitive market brings about a substantial reduction in costs of production, how will this affect the market?
p795.zh: 如果在一个完全竞争性的市场上新技术能够大幅度降低生产成本,这将如何影响市场?

p796.original: With a technological improvement that brings about a reduction in costs of production, an adjustment process will take place in the market. The technological improvement will result in an increase in supply curves, by individual firms and at the market level. The existing firms will experience higher profits for a while, which will attract other firms into the market. This entry process will stop whenever the market supply increases enough (both by existing and new firms) so profits are driven back to zero.
p796.zh: 随着技术的改进,生产成本的降低,市场将进行调整。技术的改进将使个别公司和市场的供应曲线增加。现有公司将暂时获得更高的利润,这将吸引其他公司进入市场。每当市场供应增加足够(现有和新公司),利润就会回到零时,这一进入过程就会停止。

p797.original: A market in perfect competition is in long-run equilibrium. What happens to the market if labor unions are able to increase wages for workers?
p797.zh: 完美竞争的市场处于长期平衡之中。 如果工会能够提高工人的工资,市场会怎样呢?

p798.original: When wages increase, costs of production increase. Some firms would now be making economic losses and would shut down. The supply curve then starts shifting to the left, pushing the market price up. This process ends when all firms remaining in the market earn zero economic profits. The result is a contraction in the output produced in the market.
p798.zh: 当工资增加时,生产成本就会增加. 一些公司现在将造成经济损失,并将关闭。供应曲线然后开始向左转,将市场价格推高。 当所有留在市场上的公司都赚取零经济利润时,这一进程就结束了。结果是市场产出收缩.

p802.original: Do entry and exit occur in the short run, the long run, both, or neither?
p802.zh: 进出境是短期的,长期的,两者都发生,还是两者都不发生?

p803.original: What price will a perfectly competitive firm end up charging in the long run? Why?
p803.zh: 从长远来看,一个完全具有竞争力的公司最终会收取什么价格? 为什么?

p805.original: Many firms in the United States file for bankruptcy every year, yet they still continue operating. Why would they do this instead of completely shutting down?
p805.zh: 美国的许多公司每年都申请破产,但它们仍然在继续营业。 他们为什么要这样做 而不是完全关闭?

p806.original: Why will profits for firms in a perfectly competitive industry tend to vanish in the long run?
p806.zh: 在一个完全具有竞争力的行业中,企业的利润为何会长期消失?

p807.original: Why will losses for firms in a perfectly competitive industry tend to vanish in the long run?
p807.zh: 在一个完全具有竞争力的产业中,公司的损失为何会长期消失?

p808.zh: 完全竞争性市场的效率

p809.original: When profit-maximizing firms in perfectly competitive markets combine with utility-maximizing consumers, something remarkable happens: the resulting quantities of outputs of goods and services demonstrate both productive and allocative efficiency (terms that we first introduced in Choice in a World of Scarcity).
p809.zh: 当利润最大化的企业在完全竞争的市场上与公用事业最大化的消费者相结合时,就会出现一些引人注目的情况:由此产生的商品和服务产出数量表明生产效率与分配效率(我们最初在“世界匮乏的选择”中引入的术语).

p810.original: Productive efficiency means producing without waste, so that the choice is on the production possibility frontier. In the long run in a perfectly competitive market, because of the process of entry and exit, the price in the market is equal to the minimum of the long-run average cost curve. In other words, firms produce and sell goods at the lowest possible average cost.
p810.zh: 生产效率是指无废物的生产,因此选择权在于生产可能性前沿。 从长远来看,在一个完全竞争的市场中,由于进出境的过程,市场价格等于长期平均成本曲线的最小值.换言之,公司以尽可能低的平均成本生产和销售货物。

p811.original: Allocative efficiency means that among the points on the production possibility frontier, the chosen point is socially preferred—at least in a particular and specific sense. In a perfectly competitive market, price will be equal to the marginal cost of production. Think about the price that one pays for a good as a measure of the social benefit one receives for that good; after all, willingness to pay conveys what the good is worth to a buyer. Then think about the marginal cost of producing the good as representing not just the cost for the firm, but more broadly as the social cost of producing that good. When perfectly competitive firms follow the rule that profits are maximized by producing at the quantity where price is equal to marginal cost, they are thus ensuring that the social benefits they receive from producing a good are in line with the social costs of production.
p811.zh: 分配效率意味着,在生产可能性前沿点中,选择的点是社会偏好的,至少是特定和具体意义上的。在一个完全竞争性的市场中,价格将等于生产边际成本。考虑一下作为衡量从中获得的社会福利的衡量标准,一个人为公益支付的价格;毕竟,愿意支付就意味着买方的价值。 然后考虑生产商品的边际成本,认为不仅仅是公司的成本,更广义地说是生产商品的社会成本. 如果完全有竞争力的公司遵循规则,即以价格等于边际成本的数量生产利润,从而最大限度地增加利润,它们就能够确保生产商品所产生的社会效益与生产的社会成本相一致。

p812.original: To explore what economists mean by allocative efficiency, it is useful to walk through an example. Begin by assuming that the market for wholesale flowers is perfectly competitive, and so P = MC. Now, consider what it would mean if firms in that market produced a lesser quantity of flowers. At a lesser quantity, marginal costs will not yet have increased as much, so that price will exceed marginal cost; that is, P > MC. In that situation, the benefit to society as a whole of producing additional goods, as measured by the willingness of consumers to pay for marginal units of a good, would be higher than the cost of the inputs of labor and physical capital needed to produce the marginal good. In other words, the gains to society as a whole from producing additional marginal units will be greater than the costs.
p812.zh: 为了探讨经济学家对分配效率的含意,不妨举个例子。 首先假设批发花的市场是完全有竞争力的,因此P=MC. 现在,考虑一下如果市场上的公司生产较少的鲜花会意味着什么。边际成本在数量上较低时,不会增加那么多,因此价格将超过边际成本;即P > MC。 在这种情况下,以消费者是否愿意支付某种商品的边际单位为衡量标准,生产额外商品对整个社会的好处将高于生产边际商品所需的劳动力投入和实物资本的成本。换句话说,生产额外的边际单位给整个社会带来的收益将大于成本.

p813.original: Conversely, consider what it would mean if, compared to the level of output at the allocatively efficient choice when P = MC, firms produced a greater quantity of flowers. At a greater quantity, marginal costs of production will have increased so that P < MC. In that case, the marginal costs of producing additional flowers is greater than the benefit to society as measured by what people are willing to pay. For society as a whole, since the costs are outstripping the benefits, it will make sense to produce a lower quantity of such goods.
p813.zh: 反之,如果与分配效率高的选择产出水平相比,在P=MC时,公司生产更多的花朵,则考虑这意味着什么。生产量增加,边际成本将增加,以便P < MC。 在这种情况下,生产额外花卉的边际成本大于人们愿意付出的衡量给社会带来的好处. 对整个社会来说,由于成本超过收益,生产较少的此类商品是有意义的。

p814.original: When perfectly competitive firms maximize their profits by producing the quantity where P = MC, they also assure that the benefits to consumers of what they are buying, as measured by the price they are willing to pay, is equal to the costs to society of producing the marginal units, as measured by the marginal costs the firm must pay—and thus that allocative efficiency holds.
p814.zh: 当完全有竞争力的公司通过生产P=MC的数量而最大限度地实现利润时,它们也保证,按照它们愿意支付的价格衡量,它们购买的商品给消费者带来的收益等于生产边际单位给社会带来的成本,按公司必须支付的边际成本衡量——从而保证分配效率。

p815.original: We should view the statements that a perfectly competitive market in the long run will feature both productive and allocative efficiency with a degree of skepticism about its truth.  Remember, economists are using the concept of “efficiency” in a particular and specific sense, not as a synonym for “desirable in every way.” For one thing, consumers’ ability to pay reflects the income distribution in a particular society. For example, a person with a low income may not be able to purchase their own car because they have insufficient income.
p815.zh: 我们应当审视以下说法:从长远来看,一个完全具有竞争力的市场将既具有生产效率又具有分配效率,同时对其真实性抱有一定程度的怀疑。记住,经济学家正在使用特定意义上的“效率”概念,而不是“在各个方面都可取”的同义词。 一方面,消费者的支付能力反映了特定社会的收入分配。 例如,低收入者可能因为收入不足而无法购买自己的汽车.

p816.original: Perfect competition, in the long run, is a hypothetical benchmark. For market structures such as monopoly, monopolistic competition, and oligopoly, which are more frequently observed in the real world than perfect competition, firms will not always produce at the minimum of average cost, nor will they always set price equal to marginal cost. Thus, these other competitive situations will not produce productive and allocative efficiency.
p816.zh: 从长远来看,完美的竞争是一个假设的基准。 对于垄断、垄断竞争和寡头垄断等市场结构而言,在现实世界比完美的竞争更经常地观察到,公司并不总是以最低平均成本生产,也不会总是规定价格等于边际成本。 因此,这些其他竞争情况不会产生生产性和分配效率。

p817.original: Moreover, real-world markets include many issues that are assumed away in the model of perfect competition, including pollution, inventions of new technology, poverty which may make some people unable to pay for basic necessities of life, government programs like national defense or education, discrimination in labor markets, and buyers and sellers who must deal with imperfect and unclear information. We explore these issues in other chapters. However, the theoretical efficiency of perfect competition does provide a useful benchmark for comparing the issues that arise from these real-world problems.
p817.zh: 此外,现实世界的市场包括许多在完美竞争模式中被假定为不存在的问题,包括污染、新技术的发明、可能使某些人无法支付基本生活必需品的贫困、国防或教育等政府方案、劳动力市场上的歧视,以及必须处理不完善和不明确信息的买主和卖主。 我们在其他章节中探讨这些问题。 然而,完美竞争的理论效率确实为比较这些现实世界问题所产生的问题提供了一个有用的基准。

p818.zh: 一米一分几十秒,你这混蛋!

p819.original: A quick glance at  reveals the dramatic increase in North Dakota corn production—almost a tenfold increase since 1972. Recent allocation of land to corn (as of mid-2019) is estimated to have increased to more than 4 million acres. Taking into consideration that corn typically yields two to three times as many bushels per acre as wheat, it is obvious there has been a significant increase in bushels of corn. Why the increase in corn acreage? Converging prices.
p819.zh: 粗略看一看,北达科他州玉米产量急剧增加,自1972年以来几乎增加了十倍。 最近分配给玉米的土地(截至2019年年中)估计已增加到400多万英亩。 考虑到玉米的产量一般是小麦的2至3倍,显然玉米的灌木明显增加。 为什么玉米亩增加?趋价.

p826.original: Historically, wheat prices have been higher than corn prices, offsetting wheat’s lower yield per acre. However, in recent years wheat and corn prices have been converging. In April 2013, Agweek reported the gap was just 71 cents per bushel. As the difference in price narrowed, switching to the production of higher yield per acre of corn simply made good business sense. Erik Younggren, president of the National Association of Wheat Growers said in the Agweek article, “I don't think we're going to see mile after mile of waving amber fields [of wheat] anymore." (Until wheat prices rise, we will probably be seeing field after field of tasseled corn.)
p826.zh: 从历史上看,小麦价格一直高于玉米价格,抵消了小麦每亩低产。 然而,近年来,小麦和玉米的价格一直在趋同。2013年4月,Agweek报告说,差距仅为每棵灌木林71美分. 随着价格差异的缩小,转而生产每亩玉米的较高产量就具有良好的商业意义。 全国小麦种植者协会主席Erik Younggren在Agweek的文章中说,“我不认为我们再看到一英里长的挥舞琥珀的田地[小麦]了。” (除非小麦价格上涨,我们很可能会在玉米组装后看到田地。 )

p828.original: Long-run equilibrium in perfectly competitive markets meets two important conditions: allocative efficiency and productive efficiency. These two conditions have important implications. First, resources are allocated to their best alternative use. Second, they provide the maximum satisfaction attainable by society.
p828.zh: 完全具有竞争力的市场的长期平衡满足两个重要条件:分配效率和生产效率。这两项条件具有重要影响. 首先,将资源用于最佳的替代用途。 第二,它们提供了社会所能达到的最大程度的满足。

p830.original: Productive efficiency and allocative efficiency are two concepts achieved in the long run in a perfectly competitive market. These are the two reasons why we call them “perfect.” How would you use these two concepts to analyze other market structures and label them “imperfect?”
p830.zh: 生产效率和分配效率是长期在一个完全有竞争力的市场中实现的两个概念。 这就是我们称之为“完美”的两个原因。 你将如何使用这两个概念来分析其他市场结构,并将其贴上“完美”的标签?

p831.original: Perfect competition is considered to be “perfect” because both allocative and productive efficiency are met at the same time in a long-run equilibrium. If a market structure results in long-run equilibrium that does not minimize average total costs and/or does not charge a price equal to marginal cost, then either allocative or productive (or both) efficiencies are not met, and therefore the market cannot be labeled “perfect.”
p831.zh: 完美竞争被认为是“完美”的,因为分配和生产效率同时在长期平衡中实现。 如果市场结构导致长期平衡,不能将平均总成本降到最低,和/或不收取相当于边际成本的价格,那么分配或生产性(或两者)效率都无法实现,因此市场不能被贴上“完美”的标签。

p832.original: Explain how the profit-maximizing rule of setting P = MC leads a perfectly competitive market to be allocatively efficient.
p832.zh: 解释设置P=MC的利润最大化规则如何导致一个完全具有竞争力的市场在分配上的效率。

p833.original: Think of the market price as representing the gain to society from a purchase, since it represents what someone is willing to pay. Think of the marginal cost as representing the cost to society from making the last unit of a good. If P > MC, then the benefits from producing more of a good exceed the costs, and society would gain from producing more of the good. If P < MC, then the social costs of producing the marginal good exceed the social benefits, and society should produce less of the good. Only if P = MC, the rule applied by a profit-maximizing perfectly competitive firm, will society’s costs and benefits be in balance. This choice will be the option that brings the greatest overall benefit to society.
p833.zh: 将市场价格视为代表了购买给社会带来的收益,因为它代表了人们愿意付出的代价。将边际成本视为代表了创造最后的公益单位给社会带来的成本. 如果 " P > MC " ,那么生产更多商品的好处就超过成本,而社会将受益于生产更多商品。 如果 " P < MC " ,那么生产边际商品的社会成本就超过社会效益,而社会应减少商品的产量。只有在利润最大化的完全具有竞争力的企业所实行的规则P = MC 的情况下,社会的成本和利益才会得到平衡。 这一选择将是给社会带来最大总体利益的选择。

p835.original: Will a perfectly competitive market display productive efficiency? Why or why not?
p835.zh: 一个完全具有竞争力的市场是否会显示生产效率? 为什么或为什么不呢?

p836.original: Will a perfectly competitive market display allocative efficiency? Why or why not?
p836.zh: 一个完全具有竞争力的市场是否会显示分配效率? 为什么或为什么不呢?

p838.original: Assuming that the market for cigarettes is in perfect competition, what does allocative and productive efficiency imply in this case? What does it not imply?
p838.zh: 假设香烟市场处于完美的竞争之中,在这种情况下,分配和生产效率意味着什么? 这不意味着什么?

p839.original: In the argument for why perfect competition is allocatively efficient, the price that people are willing to pay represents the gains to society and the marginal cost to the firm represents the costs to society. Can you think of some social costs or issues that are not included in the marginal cost to the firm? Or some social gains that are not included in what people pay for a good?
p839.zh: 在为什么完美竞争分配效率的论点中,人们愿意付出的代价代表了社会的收益,对企业的边际成本代表了社会的代价. 你能想到一些社会成本或问题 不包括在公司的边际成本? 或者一些社会收益,没有包括在人们为某种利益付出什么?

c1.original: Total revenue for a perfectly competitive firm is a straight line sloping up. The slope is equal to the price of the good. Total cost also slopes up, but with some curvature. At higher levels of output, total cost begins to slope upward more steeply because of diminishing marginal returns. The maximum profit will occur at the quantity where the difference between total revenue and total cost is largest.
c1.zh: 一个完全有竞争力的公司的收入总额是一条直线的斜线。坡与善价相等. 总成本也向上倾斜,但有些曲折. 在较高的产出水平上,由于边际收益减少,总成本开始急剧上升。最大利润将发生在总收入与总成本之间差额最大的数量上。

c2.original: For a perfectly competitive firm, the marginal revenue (MR) curve is a horizontal line because it is equal to the price of the good, which is determined by the market, as  illustrates. The marginal cost (MC) curve is sometimes initially downward-sloping, if there is a region of increasing marginal returns at low levels of output, but is eventually upward-sloping at higher levels of output as diminishing marginal returns kick in.
c2.zh: 对于一个完全具有竞争力的公司来说,边际收入曲线是一个水平线,因为它与商品的价格相等,而商品的价格由市场决定,如所示。边际成本(MC)曲线有时最初是向下斜的,如果产出水平低时出现边际回报增加的区域,但最终随着边际回报的减少而向上斜的输出水平较高.

c3.original: The equilibrium price of raspberries is determined through the interaction of market supply and market demand at $4.00. If there are 10 farms in the market, the equilibrium quantity is 80 × 10 = 800.
c3.zh: 浆果的平衡价格通过市场供求交互作用确定为4.00美元. 如果市场上有10个农场,则平衡数量为80×10=800。

c4.original: In (a), price intersects marginal cost above the average cost curve. Since price is greater than average cost, the firm is making a profit. In (b), price intersects marginal cost at the minimum point of the average cost curve. Since price is equal to average cost, the firm is breaking even. In (c), price intersects marginal cost below the average cost curve. Since price is less than average cost, the firm is making a loss.
c4.zh: 在(a)项中,价格相交的边际成本高于平均成本曲线。 由于价格高于平均成本,公司正在盈利. 在(b)项中,价格在平均成本曲线的最小点交叉边际成本。 由于价格等于平均成本,公司正在出现收支平衡. 在(c)项中,价格相交的边际成本低于平均成本曲线。 由于价格低于平均成本,该公司正在亏损。

c5.original: In (a), the farm produces at a level of 65. It is making losses of $47.50, but price is above average variable cost, so it continues to operate. In (b), total revenues are $90 and total cost is $165, for overall losses of $75. If the farm shuts down, it must pay only its fixed costs of $62. Shutting down is preferable to selling at a price of $1.50 per pack.
c5.zh: 在(a)中,农场产量为65级。 它的损失为47.50美元,但价格高于平均可变成本,因此继续运作。 在(b)项中,收入总额为90美元,费用总额为165美元,损失总额为75美元。 如果农场停业,必须只支付固定费用62元.关闭比每包1.50美元的售价更好.

c6.original: We can divide the marginal cost curve into three zones, based on where it is crossed by the average cost and average variable cost curves. We call the point where MC crosses AC the break even point. If the firm is operating where the market price is at a level higher than the break even point, then price will be greater than average cost and the firm is earning profits. If the price is exactly at the break even point, then the firm is making zero profits. If price falls in the zone between the shutdown point and the break even point, then the firm is making losses but will continue to operate in the short run, since it is covering its variable costs, and more if price is above the shutdown-point price. However, if price falls below the price at the shutdown point, then the firm will shut down immediately, since it is not even covering its variable costs.
c6.zh: 我们可以根据平均成本和平均可变成本曲线的跨度,将边际成本曲线分为三个区. 我们把MC穿越AC的点称为"断点"(break even point). 如果公司在市场价格高于平分点的水平上开展业务,则价格将高于平均成本,公司正在赚取利润。 如果价格正好处于平分点,那么公司就只能赚零利润. 如果在停产点和断点之间区间价格下降,那么公司正在造成损失,但在短期内将继续运作,因为它正在支付其可变成本,如果价格高于停产点价格,则价格会更高。 但是,如果在停产点价格低于价格,那么公司将立即关闭,因为它甚至无法支付其可变费用。

c7.original: In (a), demand increased and supply met it. Notice that the supply increase is equal to the demand increase. The result is that the equilibrium price stays the same as quantity sold increases. In (b), notice that sellers were not able to increase supply as much as demand. Some inputs were scarce, or wages were rising. The equilibrium price rises. In (c), sellers easily increased supply in response to the demand increase. Here, new technology or economies of scale caused the large increase in supply, resulting in declining equilibrium price.
c7.zh: 在(a)项中,需求增加,供应得到满足。注意供应增加与需求增加相等. 结果,平衡价格与销售量的增加保持不变。 在(b)项中,通知卖方不能像需求那样增加供应。 一些投入很少,或者工资正在上升。平衡价格上升。 在(c)项中,销售者根据需求的增加而容易增加供应。 在这方面,新技术或规模经济导致了供应的大幅增加,导致平衡价格下降。
